**Continuous 2.38.3**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.38.2, 2.38.1, 2.38.0, 2.36.0, 2.34.0, 2.32.0, 2.30.0, 2.28.0, 2.26.0, 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.38.3.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.38.3.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.38.3.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.38.3.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.38.3.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.38.3.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.38.3.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.38.3-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.38.3.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.38.3-vscode/continuous-cli-2.38.3.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.38.2

The model wizard shows each model's context window and lets you set it before the model is saved. Configure can read the window the model's own server lists. Several edits of one file in a turn no longer race, and switching to IDGAF clears a saved shield choice.

The extension asks a model's own server for the window that server lists. It does not contact a new host.

### Fixes

- **Context window in the wizard.** Each model row shows its published window. A checked model has the same slider and number field as Configure. Leave it blank to keep the published window. A number you set is written on that model, including one already in the config.
- **Window from the server.** Test connection reads the window and output cap a server lists (vLLM, LM Studio, OpenRouter-style, llama.cpp, Ollama) and can fill the Configure form for review. Configure asks what that model's server lists, including Bedrock Mantle. A selected model with no known window asks its own endpoint once per session instead of silently using 32,768. The picker tags those models "(Window unknown)".
- **Manage models.** The picker opens setup on the current model's connection, at its model list.
- **Edits.** Several edits of one file in a turn take a per-file lock until the diff closes. A failed apply keeps its reason.
- **IDGAF.** Switching to IDGAF clears a saved safety-check choice, so the shield follows the mode. The individual checks show off and cannot be toggled while the shield is off.
- **Shell check.** Quoted text and `~/` are not treated as a dialect mismatch.
- **Subagents.** At the call limit the run writes a report from what it found instead of returning nothing.
